puzzle.tip0: Psst… one-letter words are almost always A or I.
puzzle.tip1: Short words like THE and AND turn up a lot. Look for repeated three-letter groups.
puzzle.tip2: A single letter after an apostrophe is often S, T or D.
puzzle.tip3: Double letters? Try LL, EE, SS or OO first.
puzzle.tip4: E, T, A and O are the most common letters in English.
puzzle.tip5: Stuck? Fill in the letters you’re sure of and the rest gets easier.

aboutQuotes.title: About our quotes
aboutQuotes.p1: Every quote in LetterCrack is in the public domain. Each author died before 1956, and each quote comes from a work first published before 1929.
aboutQuotes.p2: Our main source is John Bartlett’s Familiar Quotations (9th edition, 1891). We check wording against the original texts.
aboutQuotes.p3: An editor reviews every quote before it ships. If one seems wrong or unsuitable, use Report on the puzzle menu and it will be hidden on your device.
aboutQuotes.p4: The short author notes are written by us.
